comments.body:
Design record, part 2: failure analysis and reusable pieces (part 1 is the epic description).

## Why it failed (six bug clusters, all traced to the storage and trigger design)

1. Prune-outside-the-lock: malevolent-emigratory-umbrette 3a33, eclectic-spotted-barb 3435, interior-raspberry-titi 4f8d, minced-maudlin-moth ac26, fastmoving-traitorous-magpie 4c1c, amicable-unsure-barasinga 88eb.
2. Prune breaks union-merge across clones: radical-yellowish-okapi 8185, shortish-arboreal-myotis 55bc. Removing prunes removed the only growth bound.
3. Unbounded growth and write storms: cleverish-unwitty-xanclomys 8bef, defensive-buckskin-rhino a453, eyeable-intimate-marmoset 62ab, horrendous-limpid-chamois 4eae; ADR 0106. Outcome: 105,197 of 147,074 event files (71.5%, 166 MB) were enrichment sidecars; 1,000 to 1,400 commits per hour against a 20 to 90 baseline.
4. Gate on every write is O(store): unamicable-exuberant-chupacabra 9c90, moist-short-lionfish 958e, sainted-regardable-burro f400, draughty-callous-tanager 6148, communist-metalline-cranefly a2fc; all caused_by leggy-heedless-mosquito c1de.
5. Judge unbounded and mis-contracted: sand-dominating-urus afeb, leathery-druidic-nurseshark 22da, cumbersome-littlish-koalabear d147 (the "0 findings in 2,093 reviews" measurement was a contract bug, confidence defaulted to 0.0, fixed 2026-08-12 and never re-measured before the disable).
6. Detached-child hygiene: knavish-stimulated-bluebottle aadc (a 0-byte lock blocked enrichment ~26 days), conscious-weighable-spittlebug 3198, nuclear-calm-heron da68.

Additional root cause with no ticket: the freshness key included the environment-local model string, so two environments (`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` vs `claude-opus-4-8`) re-enriched identical content in strict alternation; 93% of 23,583 consecutive digests followed no content change.

## What was sound and is reusable (by path at the commit before removal, recorded on the closing comment of the removal story under epic bossy-skittish-foal)

The digest schema and prompt; the BM25F scorer as a pure function (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/retrieve.py`); graph exclusion (`graph.py`); the judge prompt, batch contract, and both-orderings aggregation (`judge.py`); the calibration script and data (`scripts/overlap_judge_calibrate.py`, `docs/calibration/overlap_batch_confidence.md`); the content-hash freshness idea without the model string; the create-time journal (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py`) as the model for per-clone derived state.

## Recorded remediation ideas that predate this epic
apparent-sighted-cockatoo 4520 (merge-safe retention), cheerless-symphonic-eyas 475e (bound the read), unamicable-exuberant-chupacabra 9c90 option B (persistent HEAD-keyed derived index), kaput-horselike-minnow 393a and runic-felicific-sable dd37 (batch-only enrichment tiers), exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish eac3 (persistent title index; the 51-pair measurement), ADR 0106 (history reclamation of the sidecar events).

comments.body:
Architecture of the removed first implementation, moved out of the epic description to stay under the 8,000-character plan-review admission cap. No content changed.

## What the first implementation did (architecture as built; paths are at the commit before its removal, recorded on the closing comment of the removal story under epic bossy-skittish-foal)

- Enrichment: an LLM-extracted "Cupid digest" per ticket (`problem_keywords[]`, `component_or_area`, `key_entities[]`, `propositions[2..6]`; schema `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_digest.schema.json`, prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ticket_digest.md`, trivial model class) from title + description + every comment.
- Storage: the digest persisted as a signed `TICKET_DIGEST` event (~2.8 KB) in the ticket directory on the shared, auto-pushed `tickets` branch (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py`). Queue coordination also persisted as events (`ENQUEUE_ENRICH`/`CLAIM_ENRICH`/`DONE_ENRICH`, `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py`), 3 to 4 pushed commits per enrichment.
- Trigger: a drain gate on every store write (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`, `src/rebar/_store/push.py` -> `enrich_drain.maybe_drain`) spawning a detached interpreter with leases and advisory locks.
- Retrieval: brute-force BM25F over all fresh digests, rebuilt per query from a full reduce of every ticket (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/retrieve.py`; ~48 s per query on 8,938 ticket dirs, measured 2026-09-06), graph exclusion (`graph.py`), top-20.
- Judge: pairwise LLM judge over batches of 6 candidates in both orderings, both orderings must agree at confidence >= 0.7 and cite a shared artifact, at most 3 findings surfaced as ready-to-run `rebar link` commands, never auto-linked (`judge.py`; calibration `scripts/overlap_judge_calibrate.py`, `docs/calibration/overlap_batch_confidence.md`).
- Surfacing: only after a plan-review certification (`plan_review/attest.py` enqueue; `plan_review/__init__.py` `verdict["overlap"]`). Nothing ran at `create`. The only create-time check was a same-normalized-title probe over a 600 s journal (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py`), which stays.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Agents creating tickets are not shown similar existing tickets, so duplicate bugs and epics accumulate and fragment work (operator ruling 2026-09-06). The first implementation of this capability, epic only-crave-art (bd83-c56f-1f72-4ef2, ADR 0086, landed 2026-07-09/10), was switched off on 2026-08-27 (`[llm] overlap_drain = "off"`, ticket eyeable-intimate-marmoset 62ab) and 2026-08-31 (`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets = false`, ticket horrendous-limpid-chamois 4eae) because its persistence and coordination design overloaded the shared tickets branch. Its code is removed by epic bossy-skittish-foal (cea1-c784-99e0-446a); this epic is the design record and container for the replacement.

**Config state re-measured 2026-10-31.** Both switch-off citations are historical: the 13 `[llm] overlap_*` keys including `overlap_drain` are gone from `origin/main`'s `rebar.toml`, and `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is `true` but **repurposed** — it now gates only the advisory create-time same-title journal, which is the baseline AC2 must beat.

## Measured facts for the redesign

- Store: 4,285 tickets on the hot-path snapshot, 147k event files. Ticket directories were 8,960 when this epic was written; **9,778** on `origin/tickets` 1e4979b3308, of which 5,663 are live. The store grows during the epic, so size-dependent targets below track the live store rather than a frozen number.
- Duplicates worth catching are semantic. eac3 (2026-08-21) measured 51 pairs, 44 semantic, exact-title recall 14%. **That sample is superseded.** Re-derived at tickets-branch 0b9294311b5: 1,524 pairs, but **1,431 (94%) have byte-identical normalized titles** — 84 single-title clusters that are bulk-creation artifacts, not authored duplicates. The genuine set is the **93 differing-title pairs** (double eac3's 44, same kind). eac3's qualitative finding stands; its ratio does not. Pooling the strata would score near-perfect recall for the cheapest lexical method and reject vector search on an artifact.
- Paraphrase retrieval: digest-BM25F retrieved 8 of 8 heavy paraphrases at rank 1 (recall@20 = 1.0), stable from a 60- to a 200-ticket corpus, where raw-text BM25 degraded 0.875 -> 0.75 (only-crave-art derisking experiment, N = 8).
- Tickets are large: enrichment prompts reached 206k tokens before bounding (569c), so any semantic method needs summarization before embedding.
- Embeddings were rejected in July on scale grounds ("ANN pays off only >100K vectors") with N = 8; that decision is reopened by this epic.

## Operator framing (2026-09-06)

This is a vector search problem over summaries of large tickets. A lexical-only local index is insufficient and provably so against the historical corpus.

## Constraints every design must satisfy (from the 14-tool OSS survey)

- Derived search data never lives as records on the `tickets` branch; it is a disposable, version-keyed index outside the replicated store (git-bug keeps Bleve under `.git/git-bug/`; Fossil rebuilds FTS from artifacts; Cargo keys its cache by commit SHA).
- No indexing work is spawned from the write path; catch-up happens in the reader's process on next use, keyed by the tickets-branch HEAD SHA **and a format version** — two distinct triggers: a **format-version** mismatch forces a **full rebuild** (stored vectors unreadable under the new schema), while a **HEAD-SHA advance** is reconciled by an **incremental** update over only the tickets `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>` names. The ADR (AC1) fixes both; c670 already specifies this split, and the incremental path is what bounds AC4's cold-catch-up cost. A `create` is both reader and writer: its suggestion step is a read and MAY run catch-up synchronously in-process, while its event write never spawns, queues, or waits on indexing.
- Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped (3 to 5 results), and gated on a minimum title length.
- Model calls are bounded and off the write path: summarization and embedding run in a batch step or in the bounded read-phase catch-up above, never as a side effect of writing an event; an LLM judge runs only on demand over at most 10 lexical-or-vector candidates (Sentry, Discourse AI, Linear).
- Failure disposition is advisory-degrades-never-blocks: if the index is missing, catch-up or rebuild fails, the embedding surface is unavailable, or the judge errors, the suggestion field comes back empty or lexical-only with a diagnostic and the `create` still succeeds. The ADR records which tier serves each degraded case.
- The ADR's embedding model must be callable from the production Bedrock role: `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:16-17` scopes `bedrock:InvokeModel` to `anthropic.claude-*` and `infra/` holds no embedding ARN, so selecting a non-Claude model (e.g. Titan) makes adding that ARN a named gating prerequisite of the index-and-surfacing child before AC2/AC4 can pass in production.
- Correctness never depends on a daemon; the optional MCP server may pre-warm on a timer using the same code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An ADR records the chosen retrieval architecture (summarization method, embedding model and store, index location and freshness key, catch-up strategy) with measured recall@5 and recall@10 reported **per stratum and never pooled** on the stratified duplicate benchmark built from the store, committed with the tickets-branch SHA it was derived at. The architecture is justified from the **semantic** stratum; the lexical stratum is a control every candidate is expected to near-saturate. The measurements are reproducible from the committed benchmark spec. Checked by: the ADR exists under `docs/adr/` with the per-stratum tables and the exact benchmark command lines, and re-running them reproduces the tables.
- [ ] `rebar create` returns the top-5 similar existing tickets (id, alias, title, score) as an advisory field on all three surfaces (CLI `--output json`, library return dict, MCP `create_ticket` output) within a p95 of 500 ms on a synthetic store **at or above live size at implementation time** (use 10,000; live is 9,778 dirs / 5,663 tickets at 1e4979b3308; re-measured 9,780 dirs at 97c5b9ac9ab, still below the target) when the index is warm. The original 5,000 was below the live store even when written, so a target calibrated to it could pass while production was slower. Checked by: the interface parity tests plus a timing test that asserts the store size rather than assuming it.
- [ ] No derived search data is written to the `tickets` branch: after 100 creates and 100 reads on a test store, the tickets branch contains only user events. Checked by: an integration test that asserts the event-type set of the branch after the run.
- [ ] A newly created ticket is findable by the next `create` on the same clone without any background process running, via that read-phase catch-up. **The ADR (AC1) fixes the concrete mechanism and its cost**: whether catch-up embeds the backlog synchronously inside that next `create` or serves it from the lexical tier until the next batch step, and the measured p95 of a cold-catch-up `create` — AC2's 500 ms bound is scoped to a warm index and does not cover this path. Checked by: an integration test with no MCP server and no CI, plus the ADR reporting the cold-catch-up p95.
- [ ] Plan review surfaces overlap findings against the same index on demand with a bounded judge budget (at most 10 candidates, at most 2 LLM calls). Checked by: the plan-review sidecar test asserting the call count.

## Child decomposition

- Research and design (first child, roundbuilt-manlike-tapaculo): builds the stratified benchmark (1,524 pairs: 1,431 lexical / 93 semantic), measures the candidate architectures per stratum, writes the ADR. Delivers criterion 1.
- Index and create-time surfacing: delivers criteria 2, 3, 4.
- Plan-review overlap on demand: delivers criterion 5.
Children after the first are created when the ADR lands.
